retrieval_method: Research fetch_page tool across official sources on 2026-10-21 and re-verified on 2026-10-22; direct sandbox egress to non-GitHub domains is restricted. Extracts below are reviewed claims, not archived complete page bytes; additional official USGS ScienceBase, ASTER-alteration, and 3DEP product listings were reviewed on 2026-10-22, without downloading or authenticating their raster bytes.

sources.authority: DrivenData competition organizer
sources.access: read both chunks in full
verified_claims: Task: fault detection indicative of geothermal resources, not direct vent/reservoir discovery.
Initial test labels are expert-identified faults absent from the current public USGS database.
Provided numerical feature GeoTIFF is EPSG:32611 at 100 m resolution.
Distance-weighted TP is a maximum of p(x) times a triangular kernel over predictions around each truth pixel; FP uses distance to the truth; FN is truth mass minus weighted TP.
Triangular radius is 300 m; alpha is 0.2 and beta is 0.8.
Submission: single-layer float32 GeoTIFF, confidence values between 0 and 1, same CRS, resolution and bounds. Text says data outside bounds is null or NaN.
limits: Page access does not authenticate the owner-mirrored data bytes.
A local validator cannot prove remote portal acceptance.

sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey data release
sources.access: full scientific description and citation read
verified_claims: Aeroradiometric data inform surface geology and soil composition; aeromagnetic data inform subsurface structure and geology.
Area 2 nominal flight-line spacing is 400 m and tie-line spacing is 4000 m; grids at 100 m do not imply independent 100 m observations.
Magnetic processing includes tie-line levelling and micro-levelling; variable terrain clearance should be considered in interpretation.
GeoTIFF grids, CSV line data, flight-path shapefiles and processing reports are listed as release products.

Area 1 nominal height is targeted at 100 m over low relief and 150 m over mountains, with 200 m flight lines and 2,000 m tie lines; Area 2 targets 150/200 m with 400/4,000 m lines. Actual clearance can vary from the planned drape in steep terrain.
The official release listing includes contractor reports/readme, metadata CSV, flight-line CSVs, flight paths/outlines, and GeoTIFF geophysical grids.
limits: Newly estimated magnetic-marker lags do not prove displacement or fault permeability.
USGS release access is not independent confirmation that each mirrored derivative matches an original product.
The release description warns about variable terrain clearance but does not establish here that every required per-sample altitude field is available; inspect official file metadata before using it.

sources.authority: DOE Geothermal Data Repository / INGENIOUS contributors
sources.access: dataset description and resource links read
verified_claims: The compilation includes 2 m temperature probes, gravity/magnetics, heat flow, MT, faults, volcanic features, paleogeothermal features and well/spring chemistry.
Datasets are provided as is and may be redistributed with attribution; users are responsible for fitness for purpose.
Quaternary Faults v2 supersedes v1; that source is not automatically independent of the competition catalogue.

The GDR listing labels the MT contribution as electrical conductance maps and links to the separate USGS Electrical Conductance Maps release; this does not provide the specific shallow resistivity/phase-tensor slices sketched in an earlier backlog.
limits: The canonical G79-THVC lane did not require additional GDR data; no direct binary download from this host was verified in that lane.
The public listing does not establish that an MT raster is present in this repository or aligned to the competition grid.

sources.authority: Hermant, Kiersnowski & Bellanger; Stanford Geothermal Workshop 2025
sources.access: all eight parsed chunks read, including references
verified_claims: Authors use elevation, slope and Sentinel-2 B8A for fault mapping; their procedure is distinct from E1 magnetic-marker registration.
They report overfitting and fault-like paleo-shorelines, canyon margins and streams. Faults may conduct or impede fluid flow.
Their metrics are PR-AUC and weighted focal IoU; these are not competition DTI.
limits: Industry-author primary paper hosted by Stanford; not a government or organizer endorsement.
No proprietary weights, model reproduction, new data acquisition or performance transfer is claimed.

sources.access: read in full on 2026-10-22

sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey, Electrical Conductance Maps of the Great Basin
sources.access: Official ScienceBase item, summary, depth-layer names, raster extensions, and native CRS metadata read on 2026-10-22; raster bytes not downloaded.
verified_claims: The data release estimates electrical conductance from a 3D MT model and publishes five depth-integrated rasters: 2–12 km, 12–20 km, 20–50 km, 50–90 km, and 90–200 km.
The published product is conductance integrated over broad depth intervals, not 500 m / 1.5 km / 3 km resistivity slices or phase-tensor-skew rasters.
The release lists GeoTIFF rasters in native CRS EPSG:4269 and is publicly catalogued by USGS.
limits: No local binary bytes, target-footprint coverage, effective spatial resolution, or reprojection suitability were verified in this review.
A conductance anomaly is not by itself a fault, geothermal system, or permeability label.

sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey, ASTER-derived hydrothermal alteration and mineral-group map
sources.access: Official USGS Science Data Catalog metadata and product description read on 2026-10-22; thematic raster bytes not downloaded.
verified_claims: The public release maps hydrothermal alteration types, mineral groups, and green vegetation across the southwestern conterminous United States using visible, near-infrared, and shortwave-infrared ASTER data.
The released item is a thematic map product; its classes are not raw ASTER reflectance channels or direct potassium/thorium measurements.
limits: The map does not identify faults or confirm active/productive geothermal systems.
Exact footprint coverage, raster alignment, and byte hashes were not checked in this review.

sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey, Slip and dilation tendency for Quaternary faults in the Great Basin
sources.access: Official ScienceBase summary and attached-file listing read on 2026-10-22; shapefile bytes not downloaded.
verified_claims: The release provides shapefiles/KMZ for Great Basin and INGENIOUS areas and includes slip/dilation tendency results, fault geometry, and stress data used in those calculations.
The analysis is calculated for catalogue-derived Quaternary fault segments and is intended to identify orientations favorable for slip/dilation under ambient stress.
limits: The release is not a ready-made Coulomb stress raster for unknown faults.
A hide-and-recover experiment must filter/recompute strictly from fold-visible segments; precomputed held-out segment attributes would leak withheld geometry.
No local bytes or suitability for the competition grid were verified.
